(sec-item-objectgenericdae)=
# ObjectGenericDAE

A system of {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>`, {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` and algebraic equations on the coordinates of its nodes: {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` nodes, NodeGenericODE1 and NodeGenericAE, whose coordinates are the Lagrange multipliers $\tlambda$ of its algebraic equations. The linear terms are given by matrices, the nonlinear ones by user functions. NOTE that every matrix or vector must have the dimensions of the coordinates it multiplies, or be empty, using [] in Python.

## Interface

- Nodes: see the detailed description

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'GenericDAE':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | objects's unique name |
| **nodeNumbersODE2** | ArrayNodeIndex |  | [] | the nodes of the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates $\qv$, any nodes with {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates |
| **nodeNumbersODE1** | ArrayNodeIndex |  | [] | the NodeGenericODE1 of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates $\yv$ |
| **nodeNumbersAE** | ArrayNodeIndex |  | [] | the NodeGenericAE of the algebraic coordinates $\tlambda$; their number of coordinates is the number of algebraic equations |
| **massMatrix** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Mm \in \Rcal^{n_2 \times n_2}$) the mass matrix; needed if there are {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates |
| **dampingMatrix** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Dm \in \Rcal^{n_2 \times n_2}$) the damping matrix |
| **stiffnessMatrix** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Km \in \Rcal^{n_2 \times n_2}$) the stiffness matrix |
| **forceVector** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\fv \in \Rcal^{n_2}$) the constant generalized forces |
| **couplingMatrixODE1** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Em \in \Rcal^{n_2 \times n_1}$) the term of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates in the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` equations |
| **systemMatrix** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Am \in \Rcal^{n_1 \times n_1}$) the system matrix of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations |
| **rhsVector** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\gv \in \Rcal^{n_1}$) the constant right-hand side of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations |
| **couplingMatrixODE2** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Bm \in \Rcal^{n_1 \times n_2}$) the term of the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates in the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations |
| **couplingMatrixODE2_t** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Bm_t \in \Rcal^{n_1 \times n_2}$) the term of the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` velocities in the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations |
| **constraintMatrixODE2** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Cm_{\qv} \in \Rcal^{n_a \times n_2}$) the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates in the algebraic equations |
| **constraintMatrixODE1** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\Cm_{\yv} \in \Rcal^{n_a \times n_1}$) the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates in the algebraic equations |
| **constraintVector** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\cv_0 \in \Rcal^{n_a}$) the constant term of the algebraic equations |
| **parameters** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\pv_{par} \in \Rcal^{n_p}$) the parameters of the object, passed to every user function; see exudyn.advancedUtilities.ParameterLayout; empty by default |
| **forceUserFunction** | ObjectGenericDAEForceUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\fv_u \in \Rcal^{n_2}$) A Python user function which computes the nonlinear generalized forces of the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` equations |
| **rhsUserFunction** | ObjectGenericDAERhsUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\gv_u \in \Rcal^{n_1}$) A Python user function which computes the nonlinear term of the right-hand side of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations |
| **tempCoordinates** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\qv_{temp}$) the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates, kept between the calls |
| **tempCoordinates_t** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\dot\qv_{temp}$) the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` velocities, kept between the calls |
| **tempCoordinatesODE1** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\yv_{temp}$) the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates, kept between the calls |
| **visualization** | VObjectGenericDAE |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

(description-objectgenericdae)=
## Detailed description

### Coordinates

The {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates $\qv \in \Rcal^{n_2}$ are those of the nodes `nodeNumbersODE2`, the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates $\yv \in \Rcal^{n_1}$ those of the nodes `nodeNumbersODE1`, and the algebraic coordinates $\tlambda \in \Rcal^{n_a}$ - the Lagrange multipliers - those of the NodeGenericAE `nodeNumbersAE`, each in the order of the nodes; $\qv$ and $\yv$ are without the reference values. The number of algebraic equations is $n_a$.

### Equations

$$
\Mm \ddot\qv + \Dm\dot\qv + \Km\qv + \Em\yv + \Cm_{\qv}\tp\tlambda = \fv + \fv_u(mbs, t, i_N, \qv, \dot\qv, \yv, \pv_{par})
$$ (eq-objectgenericdae-ode2)

$$
\dot\yv + \Cm_{\yv}\tp\tlambda = \Am\yv + \Bm\qv + \Bm_t\dot\qv + \gv + \gv_u(mbs, t, i_N, \qv, \dot\qv, \yv, \pv_{par})
$$ (eq-objectgenericdae-ode1)

$$
\Cm_{\qv}\qv + \Cm_{\yv}\yv - \cv_0 = \Null
$$ (eq-objectgenericdae-ae)

With index 2 constraints of the solver, the algebraic equations are $\Cm_{\qv}\dot\qv + \Cm_{\yv}\dot\yv = \Null$.
The terms $\Cm_{\qv}\tp\tlambda$ and $\Cm_{\yv}\tp\tlambda$ are added by the solver from the Jacobian of the algebraic
equations, as for every constraint. CoordinateLoads are added on the right-hand side of the respective coordinate.

### Jacobians

Without user functions, every Jacobian is given by the object from its matrices. A symbolic forceUserFunction or
rhsUserFunction adds the derivatives of its recording by $\qv$, $\dot\qv$ and $\yv$, computed in one pass over the
recording (#3189); with a Python one, the Jacobian of the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` equations is computed by numerical
differentiation, with a rhsUserFunction the one of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations. The Jacobian of the algebraic equations
is always the constant matrices $\Cm_{\qv}$ and $\Cm_{\yv}$ (#3143).

### Marker interfaces

The object is no body for markers: markers act on its nodes, e.g. `MarkerNodeCoordinate`, `MarkerNodePosition` or
`MarkerNodeODE1Coordinate`, for loads, connectors or constraints on its coordinates.

**Userfunction**: `forceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, q, q_t, y, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the generalized forces $\fv_u$ on the right-hand side of the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` equations from the coordinates of the object.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the object belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs |
| `q` | Vector | $\qv \in \Rcal^{n_2}$ the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates of the object, without reference values |
| `q_t` | Vector | $\dot \qv \in \Rcal^{n_2}$ the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` velocities of the object |
| `y` | Vector | $\yv \in \Rcal^{n_1}$ the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates of the object, without reference values |
| `parameters` | Vector | $\pv_{par}$ the parameters of the object; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector | $\fv_u \in \Rcal^{n_2}$, as list or numpy array |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `rhsUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, q, q_t, y, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the term $\gv_u$ of the right-hand side of the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` equations from the coordinates of the object.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the object belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs |
| `q` | Vector | $\qv \in \Rcal^{n_2}$ the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates of the object, without reference values |
| `q_t` | Vector | $\dot \qv \in \Rcal^{n_2}$ the {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` velocities of the object |
| `y` | Vector | $\yv \in \Rcal^{n_1}$ the {ref}`ODE1 <ODE1>` coordinates of the object, without reference values |
| `parameters` | Vector | $\pv_{par}$ the parameters of the object; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector | $\gv_u \in \Rcal^{n_1}$, as list or numpy array |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

(miniexample-objectgenericdae)=
## Mini example


```python
#an oscillator x_tt + 4 x on a NodeGenericODE2 and a first order filter y_t = -y + x on a NodeGenericODE1, coupled by
#the algebraic equation x + y = 1, whose multiplier is the coordinate of a NodeGenericAE
nODE2 = mbs.AddNode(NodeGenericODE2(referenceCoordinates=[0], initialCoordinates=[0.5], initialCoordinates_t=[0],
                                    numberOfODE2Coordinates=1))
nODE1 = mbs.AddNode(NodeGenericODE1(referenceCoordinates=[0], initialCoordinates=[0.5], numberOfODE1Coordinates=1))
nAE = mbs.AddNode(NodeGenericAE(referenceCoordinates=[0], initialCoordinates=[0], numberOfAECoordinates=1))
mbs.AddObject(ObjectGenericDAE(nodeNumbersODE2=[nODE2], nodeNumbersODE1=[nODE1], nodeNumbersAE=[nAE],
                               massMatrix=[[1]], stiffnessMatrix=[[4]],
                               systemMatrix=[[-1]], couplingMatrixODE2=[[1]],
                               constraintMatrixODE2=[[1]], constraintMatrixODE1=[[1]], constraintVector=[1]))
mbs.Assemble()
mbs.SolveDynamic()

#check result at default integration time
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.systemData.GetODE2Coordinates()[0]
```
